articleTitle: Ka-Band High-Gain Omnidirectional Dual-Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work presents performance analysis of a high-gain omnidirectional dual-reflector antenna designed for operation in the Ka-band (26–40 GHz). A TEM-mode coaxial horn feeds the reflector system to ensure vertical polarization and wide operating bandwidth. A prototype was fabricated using CNC (for the reflector parts) and additive manufacturing techniques with metal and polymer plastics (for the horn feed and radome parts). The fabricated coaxial horn exhibits an impedance bandwidth (with reflection coefficient less than −10 dB) covering the entire Ka-band, and a peak realized gain of about 11.5 dBi. The complete antenna system, using aluminum reflectors and a PLA cylindrical radome, demonstrates an simulated impedance bandwidth covering the entire Ka-band and a maximum directivity of about 12.5 dBi.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Reconfigurable Bandpass Metasurfaces for Dynamic Frequency and Polarization Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work presents a reconfigurable metasurface for frequency and polarization control at S-band microwave frequencies. The structure is based on unit cells composed of complementary split-ring resonators (CSRR), namely, metallic patches and cross-shaped grids with gaps. PIN diodes are aligned along the x-axis to connect the grid, enabling bandpass frequency shifting of x-polarized waves with 1-bit keying. Numerical simulations demonstrate high extinction ratios of up to 21.71 dB and cross-talk peaks of 20.28 dB, making this design promising for future wireless communications with 1-bit reconfigurable metasurfaces.

articleTitle: A Novel Design for Compact Multiband MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact multi-band MIMO antenna design. By employing slot-coupled feeding and slotting on the radiating patch, the low-frequency mode of the antenna element is excited, achieving a miniaturized design. The proposed antenna element structure has dimensions of only 0.26λ×0.26λ, and it can generate three operating bands at 2.53 GHz, 4.73 GHz, and 7.05 GHz. The overall size of the 2-element MIMO antenna is just 0.56λ ×0.41λ, with a very compact element spacing. Simulation results indicate that the MIMO antenna achieves radiation gains of 4.3 dBi,4.0 dBi, and 6.2 dBi at 2.53 GHz, 4.73 GHz, and 7.05 GHz, respectively. The isolation at the operating frequencies is 52 dB, 15 dB, and 18 dB, respectively. This MIMO antenna features a highly compact size and excellent isolation. Index Terms—MIMO antenna, multiband, high isolation

articleTitle: Implementation of Edge Coupled Bandpass Filter on MnM Interposer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work presents an edge-coupled band-pass filter on a metallic-nanowire membrane (MnM) interposer for 60 GHz millimeter-wave (mmW) applications. The MnM interposer, utilizing nanoporous copper technology, serves as a substrate for 3D integrated circuits, enabling efficient interconnections in system-on-chip (SoC) designs. The proposed filter achieves wideband operation with simulated and measured impedance bandwidths of 6.70 GHz and 7.74 GHz, respectively, and insertion losses of 3.14 dB and 3.65 dB at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Printed Turnstile Dipole Antenna for 1U CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents an S-band antenna designed for integration with a 1U CubeSat platform. The antenna employs a modified turnstile dipole configuration above a ground plane to achieve broadside hemispherical radiation, with further enhancements made to improve bandwidth and circular polarization angular range. The final prototype measures 10 x 10 x 2.36 cm, making it ideal for 1U CubeSat installation. Performance validation demonstrates excellent impedance matching and high circular polarization purity across the 2.1-2.3 GHz band, thereby enabling reliable S-band communications for nanosatellite platforms.

articleTitle: Deployment of Private 5G Networks in Greenhouses: 26 GHz Propagation Modeling and Comparison with 3GPP Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents the characterization and modeling of 26 GHz signal propagation in a greenhouse environment using Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying (QPSK) modulation. The 26 GHz frequency, a native band in the 3GPP standards, was analyzed, and a propagation curve was modeled, leading to the derivation of a specific equation. This model was compared with established 3GPP models to evaluate the feasibility of deploying private 5G networks in agricultural settings. The unique environmental conditions within greenhouses, which can significantly affect signal performance, were considered. The results highlight key differences between the measured propagation characteristics and standard 3GPP models, emphasizing the need for tailored adjustments to optimize 5G deployments in controlled agricultural environments. These findings offer valuable insights for future 5G applications in precision agriculture.

articleTitle: An overview of 7 years of research on atmospheric propagation in Bolivia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The Radiocommunications Laboratory, a research unit of the Universidad Privada Boliviana, has been investigating on atmospheric propagation and radiometeorology since 2017. The present paper showcases an overview of the work carried out during the last seven years, as well as some of its future lines of work.

articleTitle: Broadband Dielectric Characterization of Manure and Compost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Compost and manure are crucial organic amendments derived from biomasses rich in organic matter and nutrients that enhance soil fertility and promote plant growth. This article reports a microwave dielectric characterization of manure and homemade compost in the band from 100MHz to 6GHz while using the open-ended coaxial probe technique for permittivity retrieval.

articleTitle: Reduced Size VIPIR Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Ionospheric measurement RADARs, known as ionosondes, operate in the MF and HF bands (1 MHz to 30 MHz). Vertical incidence pulsed radar (VIPIR) sends signals to be reflected by the ionosphere’s layers and captured on the ground. Due to the characteristics of power and directivity, the antennas currently used for VIPIR emission signals are very large and require expensive and complex assemblies due to their technical complements such as towers, ground systems, and lightning rods. Here is a design of a low-floor-mount spiral antenna and a ground plane for VIPIR UD transmission antenna. VIPIR UD system is an ionosonde in design that is to be reduced in size to reduce investment. The design of the antenna and ground planer is assumed from the requirements of location, gain, power management and directivity, performed on MATLAB- Antenna toolbox together with an optimization tool "surrogate model assisted differential evolution for antenna synthesis" (SADEA). The findings indicate that the proposed system meets the requirements and exceeds the directivity by as much as 6 dBi for 80% of the target band and the less structure design allows for easier assembly of the radar, requiring minor structural support and height, which reduces the budget for assembly, operation, and maintenance.

articleTitle: Experimental Indoor Measurements in a Conference Classroom at 26 GHz Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents the coverage measurements and path loss results of a 5G indoor signal within a conference classroom (Sala FIUN) located in the laboratories of the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering of the National University of Colombia. It was used an experimental setup for the measurement of path loss at millimeter wave frequencies which using mainly Sivers Semiconductors transceiver equipment and Ettus Research USRPs. The setup integrates several hardware and software components to carry out the measurements. The 26 GHz frequency was chosen for the experimental test and then the results of indoor Line of Sight (LoS) were compared with the reference models 3GPP TR 38.901, METIS and NYU finding close values between the experimental part and the reference models. These results are expected to be important to review the coverage behavior of a commercial 5G network in Colombia at the 26 GHz band millimeter wave frequency.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Patch UWB Antenna for Breast Cancer Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work evaluates the performance of an Ultra Wideband antenna designed for application on breast cancer detection systems. The development was based on a semicircular radiator patch antenna where several enhancements were implemented. The antenna was simulated and fabricated, and results showed accomplishment to the application goals. Images were reconstructed by the improved confocal algorithm employing simulated reflected signals in a system using the proposed antenna. Resulting images demonstrated feasibility of the antenna, detecting a 1.4 cm tumour in a 15.0 cm simulated breast. Preliminary results validated this antenna development toward upcoming experimental tests using real phantoms.

articleTitle: New designs and comparative analysis of multiband patch antennas for applications in C, X and Ku bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulation and analysis of a series of innovative patch antennas, focused on optimizing the use of space and materials. Through the implementation of fractal-based design techniques and other structural modifications, multiple configurations have been developed that operate in the C, X and Ku bands. The results obtained demonstrate that the proposed modifications allow achieving high gain, significantly reducing the size of the antennas and the amount of material used. In addition, the impact of various alterations in the antenna parameters has been explored, which has allowed identifying the most efficient configurations. This study contributes to the advancement in the design of compact and high-performance antennas, with various applications in these bands.

Author Keywords: FSS (Fixed Satellite Service) and DBS (Direct Broadcast Satellite) and HFSS (High Frequency Simulation Software

articleTitle: Effects of Interelement Spacing on the Input Impedance of Uniform Circular Arrays for Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) has gained popularity as a multiplexing technique. However, little emphasis has been given to the network parameters of OAM generating antennas. In this paper, we calculate the input impedance of OAM-generating uniform circular arrays (UCA) of varying radius and monopole height using 4NEC2. For tightly coupled arrays, we observed that the elements’ input impedance varies significantly as a function of both monopole height and array radius. Our simulation results can be used for future designs that consider resonant, rather than electrically small, elements for improved gain and power efficiency.

articleTitle: Flexible Ultrathin Frequency Selective Surface Dual-Band with Passband Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel ultrathin frequency selective surface with logarithmic spirals. The passband resonant frequencies of this proposed single-layer FSS are at 3.46 GHz and 10.22 GHz. A stopband with a deep null, at 6.98 GHz, separates these bands. The stopband has a bandwidth of 3.52 GHz. The −10 dB of the stopband are at 5.10 GHz and 8.62 GHz. The two passband resonances are 3.46 GHz and 10.22 GHz. The −3 dB bandwidths are 1.28 GHz and 1.62 GHz, respectively. In addition, we printed the FSS on a thin, flexible polyamide substrate. The proposed FSS has a thickness of 0.005 mm (0.0015λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength of the lower operational frequency. We compared the simulated results with the experimental ones for validation purposes. We can observe a good agreement between results.

articleTitle: Real-time Computation of E-field in Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Neuronavigation and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a brain stimulation technique used to modulate the brain activity facilitating the treatment of many psychological and morphological diseases. During TMS, it is important that we optimize the E-field dosage at the targeted brain region for efficient stimulation. A real-time TMS solver is particularly useful in this regard as it allows coil placement over the scalp on-the-fly. We introduce a method of predicting the TMS-induced E-field in under 4 milliseconds for arbitrary coil placement over the scalp. First we compute a set of orthonormal mode functions for the TMS-induced E-field using random realizations of gaussian white noise magnetic currents defined on a fictitious surface separating the head and the coil. Next, we use electromagnetic reciprocity and Huygens’s principle to compute the mode expansion coefficients. A study on 16 MRI-derived real head models reveals that the method requires only 400 modes to achieve an error of less than 2% irrespective of coil model. This enables the method suitable for real-time neuronavigation system.

articleTitle: Complex-Valued DNN for Broadband Dielectric Characterization of Dispersive Lossy Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband dielectric characterization method based on a Complex-Valued Deep Neural Network (CVNN) that allows the retrieval of permittivity and conductivity of dispersive lossy materials using ad-hoc setups. To validate the method, we numerically tested it employing a partially filled custom-made double-ridge waveguide setup, working from 0.95 to 4.2GHz. Moreover, we include a feature importance analysis using agnostic explainable-AI (XAI) techniques. The results demonstrate the flexibility and the retrieval capabilities of the method, as well as the advantages and drawbacks in comparison with traditional techniques. We publicly release the dataset and codes to support further research.

articleTitle: Human Blockage for 140 GHz Fixed Wireless Links
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: We measured human-induced blockage for a fixed wireless link at 140 GHz in a controlled indoor environment for a 5 m link distance with both the transmitter and receiver at the same height of 0.8 m. Humans of different complexities walked at a speed of 0.5 m/s on average and obstructed perpendicularly the line-of-sight of the link at different positions and thus, at different radius of the 1st Fresnel zone of the link. We found that the width of a person was inversely proportional to the observed mean attenuation, and for the same position two persons could produce fades of up to 7 dB in difference. Fade durations were well aligned with the width of each person and the average walking speed of the subjects, ranging from 470 to 660 ms in the median.

articleTitle: Simulation of Photonic Metasurfaces using a Surface Integral Equation Solver with Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Photonic metasurfaces are efficiently and accurately simulated using a surface integral equation (SIE) solver. This solver models the metasurface as an infinitesimally thin sheet on which generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) are enforced. GSTCs connect the electromagnetic fields on both sides of the metasurface using equivalent susceptibility tensors and avoid modelling of geometrically intricate metasurface unit cells by the SIE solver. Susceptibility tensors are obtained from the transmission and the reflection coefficients associated with a unit cell. A numerical example, involving a metasurface that supports high-quality factor resonances and excited by a Gaussian beam, is presented to demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Conditional Generative Algorithm for Periodic Metasurface Absorber in mm-Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This article presents the progress in the development of a generative algorithm to support the synthesis of periodic metasurfaces. The proposed model corresponds to a conditional Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (cDCGAN) to solve the backward design problem for absorptive metasurfaces. To build the training dataset, three canonical shapes were simulated in the 50-80 GHz band. The algorithm was fed with absorption spectra and additional conditions to render an image with a proposed geometry. We demonstrate that the rendered designs produce absorption profiles similar to the ground truth from the validation set, in terms of shape and absorbance. Also, the conditioning of the DCGAN works with high accuracy level. These results are promising though there is room for improvement by extending our training dataset and by delivering an operational forward network and optimization pipeline.

articleTitle: Evaluation of ITU-R P.837 rainfall rate models using high-resolution measurements in Bolivia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Rainfall rate is a key parameter in radiowave propagation, directly influencing rain attenuation prediction. This paper assesses ITU-R P.837 models that predict 1-minute rainfall rate statistics, using a 5-year high-resolution dataset of measurements in a temperate region of Bolivia as reference. Error analysis shows that the ITU-R P.837-7 model significantly outperforms previous versions, with enhanced accuracy achieved when local mean monthly meteorological data is used as input. Utilizing earlier versions of the ITU-R P.837 model may yield unreliable or inaccurate results.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Reconfigurable Metasurfaces Based on Interconnected Split Square-Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work introduces a concept for developing reconfigurable metasurfaces capable of frequency and polarization modulation within the 5G frequency range 1 (FR1) band. The design features unit cells consisting of split square-ring resonators (SSRR) interconnected exclusively along one of the primary axes, with PIN diodes linking the two sides of each SSRR. This setup allows for wavefront amplitude modulation using a 1-bit switch. Numerical simulations demonstrate high extinction ratios of up to 24.22 dB and cross-talk peaks of 22.37 dB, highlighting the potential of this design for future 5G applications through 1-bit reconfigurable metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Array Antennas Using Spherical Vector Wave Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper explores the effects of phase center translation on antenna arrays and their impact on the mode power distribution, highlighting the potential for spatial diversity. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of antenna-channel interactions, facilitating the design and characterization of intelligent communication, sensing, and localization systems.

articleTitle: Flexible UHF RFID Tag for On-Body Applications: Design and Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: There has been a substantial increase in the interest for devices directly applicable to the human body, prioritising user comfort. In this study, we developed a passive RFID tag tailored for these purposes, utilising polyimide as a flexible and low-profile substrate. The tag measures 137.80 x 27.50 mm in total and incorporates a folded dipole antenna with two integrated CSRRs to enhance its performance near the body. The maximum estimated read ranges are 3.94 m without DC input and 8.82 m with DC input on the Impinj® Monza® X-2K Dura RFID chip.

articleTitle: Investigations on a Fluidic THz True Time Delay Based on a Dielectric Slot Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband fluidic THz True Time Delay Line (TTDL) based on Dielectric Waveguides (DWGs) fabricated using High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS) in an additive 3D-printing process. The proposed design utilizes an asymmetrical mode converter, generating an air-guided field between two dielectric slabs. The structure was optimized for operation between 140 and 220GHz through full-wave simulations. The relative time delay is adjusted by filling varying amounts of fluid into the converter using a micropipette. Measurements were conducted with a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) equipped with G-band extension modules. The TTDL demonstrates a bandwidth exceeding 120GHz with low insertion loss.

articleTitle: Novel Technique for Radiation Efficiency Enhancement of Fractal Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Fractality is a well stablished method for antenna miniaturization with a myriad of papers covering fractals, quasi fractals, implementations and so. Even though, they find fewer practical applications due to its downgrade on the radiation efficiency when compared to the base form in which the fractal is applied. In this paper, we cover a "smoothing" technique to optimize the radiation efficiency of a 3.5 GHz 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> Order Square Fractal. When compared to the fractal one, the smoothed fractal radiation efficiency is enhanced by 3% absolute, and the max gain goes from 4.92dB to 5.18dB. Moreover, the smoothed fractal antenna occupies the same effective area of the unsmoothed version and is 48% smaller than the base one. More optimizations can be done for higher improvement of the fractal antenna.

articleTitle: Design Alternatives for a Submillimeter-Wave Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna with a SiGe on-chip Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this paper different alternatives for the design of a Fabry-Perot cavity antenna operating in the Sub-mmwave frequency range and fed by a SiGe spiral antenna are evaluated. In particular a single spiral and a sequentially fed array of spiral antennas are compared, showing, due to the losses in the Si substrate the superior performance of the single fed cavity. However, the use of a sequentially rotated array significantly improves the Axial Ratio (AR).

articleTitle: Statistical Performance Prediction of SatCom Systems Featuring Smart Gateway Diversity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The shift of current satellite systems towards higher bands prompts for fade mitigation techniques such as Smart Gateway Diversity (SGD) to meet typical availability targets. This paper compares feeder link simulations of a conventional Ka-Band system (no SGD), with Q/V- and, as a novelty, W-band systems featuring SGD. The aim is to calculate the system margin, i.e. the extra transmit power w.r.t. free-space propagation, required to maintain the same number of gateways and the same system availability in the three systems. In a European scenario, a W-band system would require a margin 5.6 dB higher than an equivalent Q/V-band system with 6 gateways and one back-up.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Dual-Band Reflectarray with a 3D Metallic Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This contribution introduces a novel design of a dual band 3D fully metallic unit cell intended for use in reflectarray configurations for satellite communication applications. The main novelty of this research lies in the application of the geometric phase principle to achieve a unit cell capable of independently controlling the phase of the reflection coefficient in two distinct frequency bands (20 and 30 GHz) while maintaining high polarization purity. We also propose an efficient analysis approach for the final dual reflectarray configuration using a combination of geometrical optics and physical optics, providing both good accuracy and numerical efficiency for electrically large structures.

articleTitle: Measurement Campaign for 5G Communications in Greenhouse Scenarios: Tropicario Jardín Botánico de Bogotá José Celestino Mutis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: A measurement campaign was developed to determine how path loss models proposed for 5G by Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) are applicable in Greenhouse scenarios. This campaign was focused on mm waves regime, so 28 GHz frequency was used. In order to accomplish that, a wireless transmission system was developed, measurements were taken in the Tropicario greenhouses at Jose Celestino Mutis Botanical Garden, setting different distances and orientations.

articleTitle: Parabolic Equation Numerical Solutions Applied in Long-Range and Realistic Propagation Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper applies Split Step Parabolic Equation (SSPE) and Finite Difference (FD) algorithms in radiopropagation problems. Both techniques were tested in long-range cases for fifth generation (5G) frequency bands, when used to provide broadband connectivity in rural and suburban areas. The results showed that the conjuction of the Discrete Mixed Fourier Transform (DMFT) with SSPE offers an efficient response compared to FD method in canonical and realistic scenarios. This research also presents that DMFT-SSPE is a promising approach to analyze 5G radio links in mountainous and humidity regions.

articleTitle: Directional Measurements in an Indoor Corridor under Line-of-Sight Conditions at 140 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Achieving adequate coverage with high-gain antennas is crucial for fully utilizing the mmWave and sub-THz bands. This study reports indoor measurements at 140 GHz in Line-of-Sight (LOS) conditions within a corridor using a narrowband channel sounder. A 10° (24 dBi) receive horn antenna on a rotating platform and a 50° (10 dBi) transmit antenna were used. Path gain was modeled with a power-law, yielding an RMS error of 1.75 dB. Scattering degraded azimuth gain by up to 2.82 dB in the corridor with 90% probability.

articleTitle: Development of a Satellite Meteorological Image Reception and Decoding System Using Software-Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This scientific paper presents the experimental results obtained from implementing an integrated system for the reception and decoding of meteorological satellite images based on Software Defined Radio (SDR). This system was designed to address the lack of low-cost and accessible climate data for future meteorological and climatological studies. The characteristics of sun-synchronous orbit satellites were analyzed, and the necessary components for the development of the image reception system were identified. Additionally, an efficient database was established to systematically store the acquired image records. Detailed tests verified the efficiency and functionality of the system in receiving and processing satellite data, confirming that the obtained images are comparable to those provided by recognized external services, thus validating the feasibility and utility of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Microwave-based Hyperthermia system to evaluate Cell-Death in Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This article presents a microwave-based hyperthermia (HT) setup to evaluate the temperature profile distribution over a breast fat phantom and cellular death on spheroids of the line MCF-7. The setup is composed of an illumination system and a temperature measurement system that allows to characterize the process. Spheroids of the MCF-7 line were incubated, with a diameter of 0.5 cm. Cell death was evaluated at temperatures of 38, 41, 43 and 45 °C, achieving cell death by apoptosis in the last 2 cases.

articleTitle: Frequency Behavior of a Resonant Shielded Loop With a Variable Gap Position
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Size and bandwidth are among the most common tradeoffs in antenna design. Electrically small antennas (ESAs) suffer from low radiation resistance, high reactance, and typically narrow bandwidths. Resonant antennas offer a higher radiation resistance lower and input reactance than ESAs at the cost of a larger footprint. Shielded loops offer a compromise between bandwidth and size. We observed that S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> is minimum when the electrical length between the gap and the short from inner to outer conductor is λ/4. The frequency behavior depends on this gap position rather than the overall loop radius.

articleTitle: An Ultra Thin Flexible Super Wideband Antenna Using Additively Manufactured Elastomer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this paper, an ACS (asymmetric coplanar strip line) fed printed monopole antenna is proposed. The antenna is realized on the low cost FR4 substrate. An additively manufactured elastomer is integrated with the printed monopole, to enhance the flexibility of the antenna. The proposed antenna offers an impedance bandwidth of 126% with quasi omnidirectional patterns throughout the operating band. The proposed antenna is characterized for conformity; the performance metrics of the proposed antenna remain agnostic to bending.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly-Polarized Gap Waveguide-Based Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an all-metal antenna based on Gap Waveguide technology. The antenna, which is realized using a Ridge Gap Waveguide, consists of just two layers, maintaining a compact size. The first layer is made up of two perpendicularly placed arms, which comprise the feeding, and the second layer hosts a diamond shaped slot and a horn, which comprise the radiator. Simulations show that the design achieves a remarkable bandwidth equivalent to the 31.43% of the central frequency in terms of both S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameter, being below -10 dB, and Axial Ratio, being below 3 dB.

articleTitle: Channel utilization in the ISM 5 GHz band. Case study city of Ocaña, Colombia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: 5G technologies are critical for digital transformation, as they provide the connectivity needed to implement new communication solutions and connect a wide range of devices, including people, sensors, and machines. This can lead to channel congestion and decreased connection speed and quality. In addition, the 5 GHz ISM frequency band has a more limited range than other lower frequency bands. This can be a problem in environments where a long-distance wireless connection is required, such as in large buildings or university campuses. Efficient utilization of the channels in the 5 GHz band is essential to minimize interference and ensure optimal data transmission performance. However, this is not always possible due to the many devices and services sharing this frequency band. A study is conducted to establish the best frequency bands and best practices where the established standards are met for better efficiency in terms of channel utilization by service providers in the city.

articleTitle: Modeling Propagation Loss at 5.8 GHz: A Comparison of Log-Distance Models and Machine Learning with Empirical Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This study evaluates several propagation loss models by comparing them with empirical data collected from measurement campaigns at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUCRio) at a central frequency of 5.8 GHz. The analysis covers five models: the Free Space Path Loss (FSPL) model, the Log-Distance Path Loss Model (LDPM), the Log-Distance Path Loss Model with Shadowing (LDPM-S) with fixed parameters (n=3, =6), LDPM-S with parameters obtained empirically, and the ADAM algorithm for machine learning. The results demonstrate that the ADAM algorithm achieved significantly higher accuracy than the traditional deterministic models, highlighting its potential to enhance performance in path loss estimation.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Wideband 8-Element Series-Feed Array on Metallic-Nanowire-Membrane Interposer for Millimeter Wave Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to present an 8-element wideband series-fed array antenna fabricated on a metallic-nanowire-membrane (MnM) interposer for 60 GHz millimeter-wave applications. The MnM interposer, based on nanoporous technology filled with copper, serves as an novel substrate with high potential for 3D integrated circuits due to the ease of creating through-substrate vias (TSV) and interconnections between microwave components and system-on-chip (SoC). The results demonstrate a wideband frequency with adequate impedance matching of 19.48 GHz (simulated) and 23.80 GHz (measured).

articleTitle: Thermal Validation of a Novel Antenna Design for Superficial Microwave Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: We present the design and thermal validation of an antenna to administer superficial hyperthermia to treat melanoma. This applicator antenna is based on the double folded dipole with modifications to better control the size and shape of thermal footprint in the skin and beneath. This design is lightweight and compact, is easy and affordable to manufacture, and may be integrated into complex systems. Experimental results on a human phantom show that our design generates a heating area and intensity appropriate for the hyperthermia treatment of melanoma.

articleTitle: Assessment of Signal-to-Clutter Ratio Improvement using TX Beamforming on Cascade FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The dynamic range of radar receiver chains is a critical concern in practical scenarios due to the significant variation in power levels between backscattered signals from desired targets and surrounding clutter. High Radar Cross Section (RCS) clutter echoes can easily overwhelm the receiver chain, particularly when the detection system is optimized for low RCS targets, such as UAVs or birds. This paper explores the potential enhancements offered by TX Digital Scanning Beamforming compared to conventional MIMO techniques. It introduces a straightforward model to predict these benefits, supported by an experimental validation using a Texas Instruments (TI) FMCW Cascade Radar platform operating in TX Beamforming mode, offering valuable insights into the achievable performance improvements.

articleTitle: Multipole Decomposition Method for Tailoring Multiband Microwave Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work demonstrates that the multipole expansion method can be effectively applied to the scattered fields of unit-cell elements in frequency selective surfaces to accurately reproduce their transmission properties. Additionally, our analytical approach reveals that multiband behavior can be achieved by combining different elements (with nearby resonances) within the unit cell. Importantly, the multipole expansion allows for identifying individual contributions from each multipole to the spectra, paving the way for future studies that could exploit interactions between these modes to design and fine-tune FSSs with desired features.

articleTitle: Dynamic Beamforming with Microfluidic-Based Digitally Coded Microwave Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: We present a microfluidic-based, digitally-coded reconfigurable metasurface for dynamic beamforming applications. The structure is designed using conventional materials and fabrication methods commonly used in microfluidic and radio frequency devices, demonstrating the feasibility of the concept in this work. As a result, we successfully achieved the splitting of the incident field into two tilted, mirror-symmetric beams, unlike conventional reflectors, which only reflect a single beam back in the direction of propagation.

articleTitle: Material Characterization for Phantoms in Microwave SAR Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this study, a tissue-equivalent phantom was fabricated and characterized to evaluate the specific absorption rate (SAR) in microwave hyperthermia applications. Initially, both static and dynamic thermal properties, including thermal conductivity and specific heat capacity, were analyzed, while electromagnetic properties such as permittivity and conductivity were determined using the coplanar waveguide method. The results indicate that the phantom effectively replicates the properties of human tissue, enabling realistic simulations and advancing research on hyperthermia treatment through enhanced thermal and electromagnetic characterization.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Cochlear Implant Exposure to Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The following research gives an experimental assessment of the exposure of cochlear implants to electromagnetic fields. To do so, a phantom of the human body and a model of a cochlear implant were used. After analyzing a crucial case of electromagnetic exposure to an Implantable Medical Device (IMD), it was discovered that the electric fields surrounding it are in compliance with existing regulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Experimental Bias Voltage Generation for RIS Using Standing Wave Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: We present an advancement in the experimental generation of dc voltage for biasing varactors on a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) using a novel technique named "wave control". The method consists of using a single cable that delivers a time-domain periodic waveform which creates standing waves on a biasing transmission line beneath the RF surface. This can enable dynamic control of the dc voltage distribution across the RIS.

articleTitle: Dual-Band MIMO Antenna for 5G Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band four-element multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) antenna system based on resonant rings with different feeding is proposed for the fifth-generation (5G) operation in mobile terminals. According to the simulation results, the MIMO antenna system is optimized to operate in both 2.3 GHz and 3.5 GHz bands with reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>-parameter) better than -20 dB. The simulation results were validated with measurements obtaining a dual-band MIMO antenna.

articleTitle: A Dual-Beam Frequency-Scanning Antenna Based on Surface-Wave Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a dual-beam frequency-scanning antenna based on a surface wave power divider. The surface wave transmission line structure for the power divider is designed by developing a complementary groove plasmonic transmission line structure and a transition between the groove plasmonic transmission lines. Periodic radiation patches are added to the surface wave transmission line to achieve coupling and conversion from surface waves to radiated electromagnetic waves, thereby realizing the dual-beam frequency-scanning antenna. Simulation results show that the antenna has two radiation beams on the left and right, its radiation beam scanning angle can cover ±45 degrees with the frequency of 8.8 GHz-11.2 GHz. As the frequency increases, the two radiation beams deflect toward the center. At 11.2 GHz, the phase of the units in both directions aligns, leading to beam combination with a maximum gain of 14.5 dBi. Furthermore, at 11.4 GHz, the two beams begin to deflect in opposite directions, and a wide beam is achieved at this frequency. The antenna has the advantages of simple structure and low profile.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Estimation of Canonical Targets in a Simulated Reverberation Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper studies the feasibility of estimating the radar cross-section (RCS) pattern of canonical targets inside a reverberation chamber simulated with the FDTD method.

articleTitle: The use of NYUSIM for Path Loss Characterization in an Urban Microcell Environment for IoT-5G at 3.5 GHz Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this paper, we use the open-source MATLAB-based NYU Channel Model (NYUSIM) simulator to analyze the path loss propagation behavior at 3.5 GHz in an urban microcell (UMi) scenario and thus compare the values that we obtained for the path loss exponent (PLE) in a corridor scenario based on an extensive measurement campaign. These PLE values can be used in simulation tools to evaluate the path loss behavior and optimize the implementation of device and sensor network infrastructure to enable IoT-5G connectivity.

articleTitle: Fast Computation of the EM Effect of Small Defects on Large Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Aircraft and vehicles often have small surface imperfections like protruding rivets or tiny holes. Despite being smaller than the wavelength of the impinging waves, these imperfections can significantly affect the electromagnetic field induced into the vehicles and scattered by them. However, analyzing these imperfections using the method of moments presents challenges, especially in mesh generation and numerical simulation. The paper shows that accurately reproducing the impact of these imperfections on the field is possible by adding small RWG basis function “patches” to a smooth mesh that does not include the imperfections. These patches enable the evaluation of electric and magnetic currents through the appropriate polarizabilities.

articleTitle: Prediction of Path Loss in Real-World Environments: Comparison of ITU-R P.1411 Models and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Accurate path loss estimation is essential for the design and optimization of wireless networks, especially in urban environments where propagation conditions can be extremely variable. This study compares traditional models such as the Free Space Path Loss (FSPL) model, ITU-R P.1411 model, and ITU-R P.1411 model with obstacles with an advanced machine learning approach using the ADAM algorithmEmpirical data were collected on the campus of the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUCRio) at a frequency of 5.8 GHz. The comparison between the methods revealed that the machine learning approach offers greater accuracy, surpassing traditional deterministic models in terms of path loss estimation accuracy .

articleTitle: Patch Antenna for Microwave Thermal Therapy of Melanoma
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and validation of a compact patch antenna for microwave hyperthermia treatment of melanoma. Operating at 2.45 GHz, the antenna achieves a focused electric field, ensuring effective treatment of melanoma lesions with minimal impact on surrounding tissues. Simulations and experimental tests with a human phantom show compatibility with typical melanoma lesion sizes and confirm the design’s feasibility. The low-cost, easy-to-manufacture antenna is a promising tool for clinical use.

articleTitle: The Lower Hybrid resonance effect in the simulation of Ion-Cyclotron plasma heating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The TOPICA (TOrino Polytechnic Ion Cyclotron Antenna) code is an advanced tool for simulating ion-cyclotron (IC) radio frequency antennas. This document presents a study based on simulations of the lower hybrid (LH) resonance effect in the TOPICA code. The document briefly explains the lower hybrid resonance problem, describes the simulation setup, and presents the results in terms of electric field distribution. Additionally, we propose a possible approach to identifying the problem.

articleTitle: Coexistence Studies Between 5G and TV Service in the 600 MHz Band in Colombia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: 5G technology goes one step beyond mobile connectivity by allowing far more devices to access the mobile internet at the same time, such as objects, sensors, vehicles, and machines. On the other side, to improve coverage in rural areas, in order to connect the unconnected and underconnected is a goal, and the second digital dividend is a way proposed to reach this goal. Considering that the 5G commercial is starting, it will be necessary to evaluate the impact for deploying 5G mobile networks in the 600MHz band, also known as the second digital dividend, which are one of the new bands. In this paper, the aim is to define the technical operating parameters that guarantee the coexistence and 5G systems deployment with the DTV service in the 600MHz band. The results have been obtained by laboratory measurements using professional and commercial equipment in a controlled environment. In fact, laboratory measures allowed to obtain Protection Ratios (PR), to ensure operation between 5G and DTV technologies, from co-channel to adjacent band

articleTitle: Vivaldi Antipodal Antenna with triangular slots fed by air-filled RSIW for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)

authors.preferredName: Priscilla Kadja P. de M. Carneiro

abstract: This paper presents a modified Vivaldi antipodal antenna using air-filled RSIW technology for UWB applications. The structure has a triangular slot edge, extending the bandwidth and increasing the gain. A prototype of the modified antenna was simulated and fabricated. The measured results show reasonable agreement with simulations, validating the design procedure. The proposed antenna offers a low-cost, easy-to-manufacture and compact solution. Additionally, improvements in performance were observed, including a 1 GHz increase in bandwidth and an additional 1.58 dB in gain, compared to the antenna using only the RSIW technology.

articleTitle: Assessing MIMO and Beamforming for Low RCS UAV Detection via Radar Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Detecting low Radar Cross Section (RCS) targets like UAVs demands advanced radar technologies with high resolution and sensitivity. This study evaluates Beamforming and MIMO radar technologies for their effectiveness in detecting low RCS targets, emphasizing range, angular resolution, and Doppler sensitivity. By integrating Digital Twins, the study bridges simulation and real-world environments, showing that Beamforming enhances detection in noisy conditions by optimizing SNR. Meanwhile, MIMO performs better in range resolution and Doppler sensitivity. The strong match between Digital Twins and real-world tests confirms their accuracy and importance.

articleTitle: Evaluation of total precipitation from ERA5-Land reanalysis for rain attenuation studies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Propagation researchers continuously seek rainfall data to enhance rain attenuation modeling. This paper compares 60-to-1 minute converted long-term rainfall statistics from ERA5-Land reanalysis with experimental measurements from two rain sensors and ITU-R predictions for a specific region in Bolivia. Despite improved spatial resolution, discrepancies arise due to time resolution and grid averaging.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm for Amplitude Enhancement in Circular Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of optimizing radiation patterns for a virtual antenna arrays in a Flying Ad-hoc Network (FANET), a critical factor in improving communication system performance. We present a genetic algorithm approach for optimizing the amplitudes of a six-element antenna array arranged in a hexagonal geometry. The methodology combines principles of circular geometry with evolutionary computation, utilizing a fitness function that evaluates the array factor and a dipole element. Our genetic algorithm, demonstrates significant improvement in antenna performance. This approach showcases the potential of genetic algorithms in antenna design automation, offering improved performance and insights into optimal array configurations for FANET applications.

articleTitle: A Matryoshka-like Geometry Planar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper introduces a matryoshka-like geometry planar antenna, MTK-LA. The matryoshka-like geometry was described, including initial design equations. To verify the expected characteristics, a prototype operating at 199 MHz was designed, fabricated and characterized, verifying a good agreement between numerical and measured results. One of the most interesting features observed was the reduced dimensions, achieving an overall dimension of 0.033λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ×0.033λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. Despite the MTK-LA be especially attractive for low frequency application, its dimensions can be adjusted and applications at high frequencies are also possible.

articleTitle: Comparing Exponential Decay Models for Path Loss Prediction at 5.8 GHz Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Accurate path loss estimation is crucial for optimizing wireless networks, particularly in urban environments where signal propagation is complicated by factors such as buildings and vegetation. This study evaluates the performance of traditional path loss models against an AI-based approach utilizing the ADAM optimization algorithm. Data collected at 5.8 GHz from the Pontificia Universidade Catolica do Rio de Janeiro (PUCRio) campus, characterized by significant vegetation and six-story buildings. These findings underscore the potential of integrating advanced techniques into the design and optimization of wireless networks to enhance accuracy and communication performance.

articleTitle: Simplified Multi-Channel Calibration for Microwave Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work proposes and validates a simplified n-channel calibration for microwave imaging systems that reduces the complexity of a standard full-port calibration from a minimum of 4n − 1 measurements to 4(2) 1 ones, respectively. The method consists of a joined 2-port −standard calibration with a multi-port extrapolation. It compensates for systematic errors and mitigates the effects of losses and phase shifting caused by the multiplexing stage of a microwave imaging system. The conditioning and limitations of the technique are studied, including the switching matrix’s dynamic range, insertion loss, and the error path extrapolation analysis. Finally, the calibration is validated by employing a brain stroke monitoring system using either an electromechanical switching matrix or a solid-state-based one, and repeatability and stability tests that demonstrate the calibration’s effectiveness and robustness are performed.

articleTitle: True Rays Model Integration in OMNeT++ for IIoT Network Planning in Underground Mines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work develops a new module in the OMNeT++ simulator incorporating and validating the True Rays propagation model for underground environments. The integration enables the planning and evaluation of Industrial Internet of Things deployments of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) in mining scenarios. The tool can read the mine blueprints and deploy nodes at specified locations. It also defined the environment and network communication parameters for network coverage and performance analysis, allowing an understanding of how the WSN behaves in the underground mine before its deployment. The simulation predicts variables such as received power and path losses, optimizing sensing coverage and connectivity while reducing the need for site surveys. A large number of simulations using blueprints from real mines show that the signal propagation measurements are consistent with the theoretical models proposed in the state of the art. Experimental results were compared with a simulation WSN using LoRa, the maximum range obtained in simulation was 47 m, the measurements under real conditions in the underground only achieved 25 m of reach, but were limited at a threshold of -100 dBm to ensure connectivity and reliability of transmission among the nodes. As a result, the simulations and measurements performed better at the 433 MHz frequency, and the main contribution is a simulation tool simplifying planning IIoT networks in mining tunnels.

articleTitle: Rain Attenuation at mmWave Using Visibility Data: A Case Study for Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) technology offers high data rates for 6G networks but is affected by rain. This paper evaluates a visibility-based method for estimating rain attenuation in mmWave links, using data from CEDA and DBSG-3 ITU-R. The model shows good agreement at 57 and 137 GHz, making it useful in locations with limited rain data but accessible visibility measurements, such as airports. Future work will focus on refining and expanding the model’s applicability.

articleTitle: Modeling Tidal Fading with the Two-Ray Model for Short-Range WiFi Overwater Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This research evaluates the two-ray propagation model as a tool for predicting tidal fading over short-range overwater WiFi links. We compare the accuracy of the i) full version of the two-ray model, which considers a material (e.g., relative permittivity) and polarization-dependent reflection coefficient, against the ii) simplified —yet widespread— two-ray model with a reflection coefficient magnitude of one. The evaluation is done resorting to a real-world dataset of a Shore-to-Shore (S2S) WiFi communication link operating in the 2.4 GHz band over an intertidal zone during an ebb period of about 2.5 h. The results show a clear agreement between received signal strength measurements and the full two-ray model, achieving a root mean square error below 1 dB. Overall, the work stresses the importance of using the complete two-ray model incorporating relative permittivity and antenna polarization in overwater communication modeling.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Ion Cyclotron Antennas for Nuclear Fusion Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In nuclear fusion experiments, one of the most assessed methods for heating plasma is via transfer of electromagnetic energy in the Ion Cyclotron Resonance Frequency (ICRF) range. However, space constraints for the plasma-facing antennas result in poor impedance matching and high electric fields; for these reasons current antennas cannot efficiently couple high power to the plasma and require complex matching circuits. This preliminary study presents a new perspective on designing tunable resonant antennas, based on quarter-wavelength resonances.

articleTitle: SEM-Based Analysis of Electromagnetic Logging Sensors for Oil Wells in Geophysical Formations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work introduces a new formulation for modeling electromagnetic well-logging sensors using the higher-order spectral element method. The approach utilizes the Lorentz reciprocity theorem to determine the total field generated by practical sources. Horizontal coil antennas are used for both the sensor’s transmitter and receiver. The method is tested in an oil invasion zone scenario, and preliminary results align well with the mode-matching technique reference solutions.

articleTitle: About Antenna Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper will establish proof that physical identical transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) antennas do not have the same characteristics properties in a radio link in free space and over ground, although in certain limited cases they appear to be the same.

articleTitle: Empirical Evaluation of the Two-Ray Model for mmWave Overwater Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Understanding and characterizing millimeter wave (mmWave) communication in real-world scenarios is crucial to design reliable communication systems for Internet of Things (IoT) applications, including autonomous vessel’s remote operation. To this aim, this research provides an empirical evaluation of large-scale fading for vessel-to-shore communication at 28 GHz. Specifically, we experimentally assess the path loss (PL) performance of short-range Line-of-Sight (LoS) links with low antenna heights. The measurements show trends that match well with the two-ray model PL predictions, yielding a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.56 dB in the 10-100 m range.

articleTitle: Construction and testing of the MIST antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This article presents the construction and testing of the MIST (Mapper of the IGM Spin Temperature) antenna, a blade dipole optimized for radio astronomy in the VHF band. The antenna is made of solid aluminum panels and supported by fiberglass structures, operating without a metallic ground plane. For testing, reflection coefficient measurements were conducted at three different locations in Concepción, Chile. The results show a consistent resonant feature at 50 MHz. The portability of the MIST antenna and instrument makes them suitable for conducting observations from diverse remote locations. The main scientific objective of MIST is detecting the faint 21-cm signal produced by neutral hydrogen gas during the dark ages and cosmic dawn of the Universe.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Frequency-Selective Surface with Closely Resonant Bands inspired by the Oxalis tetraphylla
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) inspired by the shape of Oxalis tetraphylla for applications with closely resonant bands for WLAN and 5G communication systems. The numerical results obtained were two frequencies: 2.41 GHz with a bandwidth of 420 MHz and 3.47 GHz with a bandwidth of 180 MHz. In the measurements, the frequencies were 2.44 GHz with a bandwidth of 330 MHz and 3.47 GHz with a bandwidth of 130 MHz, respectively. The FSS showed angular stability and polarization insensitivity for oblique angles up to 30°.

articleTitle: Jammer Localization Using Time Difference of Arrival Algorithm in 5G Mobile Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Jammers are electronic devices engineered to disrupt radio frequency communications by transmitting a broadband noise signal across a specific bandwidth. This paper presents a method using 5G technologies to determine the transmitter’s location by processing the signal received by multiple antennas. Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) algorithms estimates the jammer’s position within a controlled environment. The experimental results demonstrate high accuracy, with Root Mean Square Errors (RMSE) consistently below 0.25 meters. This level of precision highlights the method’s potential to enhance the resilience of future 5G networks against jamming threats. These findings underscore the effectiveness of integrating TDOA-based localization techniques in 5G networks for proactive jamming detection and mitigation.

articleTitle: A CORPS Beamforming Network for Time Modulated Circular Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper presents a CORPS beamforming network for a Time Modulated Circular Array. The design of the CORPS network allows to reduce the number of Time Modulators needed to perform beam-steering in the azimuth and elevation planes, while keeping a low sideband radiation. Full wave simulation of the CORPS network is presented to validate the proposed design.

articleTitle: High-Gain Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna Array based on ENZ Medium for Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work proposes a high-gain waveguide-fed cavity-backed slot antenna array based on ENZ medium for millimeter wave operation. The array’s elements comprise a metallic cavity doped by FR4 dielectric slabs surrounded by four metallic rods to achieve an ENZ medium. The array’s elements were excited by a T-junction 4:1 power divider fed by a commercial single waveguide-to-coaxial transition through a standard WR28 waveguide. Two symmetrical wing-based reflectors were also applied to the array for gain increment. The array full-wave numerical analyses results show a bandwidth of 630 MHz (26.04 26.67 GHz), a gain of 22.12 dBi, side lobe levels below 14.67 dB, and radiation efficiency of 49.88%.

articleTitle: Rectangular Phased Array Scanning Loss Error When the Active Element Patterns are Calibrated at Boresight or Approximated by a Unit-cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Designing phased arrays is simplified by assuming the elements have a common pattern, often the infinite array unitcell or average active element pattern. A similar approach can simplify the phased array calibration, where all the variations between the RF front-end electronics are calibrated out using a single beam direction and the element patterns are assumed to be identical. This paper presents the error in the steered realized gain for a rectangular patch phased array when the active element patterns are approximated using an infinite array unit-cell pattern. The impacts on the realized gain from using a simple boresight gain and phase calibration are also presented. All results are derived from simulation.

articleTitle: Path Loss Measurements in the 60 GHz Frequency Band in a Greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This study characterizes path loss in the 60 GHz band in a tomato greenhouse and reveals significant losses due to ambient and vegetation. The experimental results are compared to applicable propagation models, showing varying levels of correspondence and achieving a satisfactory theoretical description. The findings improve the understanding of millimeter wave propagation in agricultural environments, which can support 5G network deployments.

articleTitle: Empirical Validation of the MTW Fading Model for Extreme Parameter Values
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: It is shown that the MTW fading model provides very good fitting results to empirical data obtained in harsh propagation scenarios when its parameters take extreme values.

articleTitle: Accelerated Quantum Selection Optimization of a Microwave Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Optimization techniques have long been employed in designing electromagnetic structures. With the emergence of quantum computing, hybrid quantum-classical optimization algorithms are appearing as promising solutions. This paper presents a new approach that integrates quantum algorithms with classical optimization to profit from the advantages of both quantum and classical computing.

articleTitle: Applications of the extension of the method of images under low loss ground plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The method of images is well-known in electromagnetic radiation problems, like currents on a metallic ground plane to replace the original problem. This paper extends the method of images to the case of a dipole antenna on a dielectric ground plane, like concrete, considering that from 1 GHz to 70 GHz is a low-loss dielectric material. The contribution of this paper is the model that expresses the electric and magnetic fields through the method of images for a dipole on a dielectric ground plane, for vertical and horizontal polarization for high frequencies mobile communications services. The impact of this extension of the method of images developed by W. G. Fano can be very important since many times statistical models are used with cost is tens of thousands of dollars, however here something much simpler and very low cost is proposed. Antennas over dielectric ground plane can be as well computed theoretically.

articleTitle: Validation of a Freehand Tri-Axial Field Measurement Setup for 3D Domains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: We present a manual system for measuring the spatial distribution of the electric field, suitable for evaluating the compatibility and bio-compatibility of radiating electromagnetic systems. The system demonstrates the capability to measure the magnitude of the three components of the electric field downto 27 dBV/m, with a sampling rate of 60 Hz and a spatial error of less than 1 mm. The comparison with simulations at a frequency of 5.8 GHz shows good accuracy and dynamic range in a user-friendly system.

articleTitle: 3D-printed Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Omnidirectional Radiation Pattern and Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This article presents the design of a dielectric resonator antenna with an omnidirectional radiation pattern and circular polarization for UAV aplications. The antenna is composed of a dielectric cylinder with two counter-rotating helices to be implemented using 3D-printing technology. Simulation results shows a maximum gain of 2.4 dBi and an axial ratio below 3 dB over the impedance bandwidth of the antenna.

articleTitle: On the Accuracy of Truncated Pattern Stitching with Directional Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: Using a double-ridged horn antenna as a case study, this paper examines the accuracy of a previously proposed pattern stitching method with directional antennas. Using various mounting configurations, scaled mean square error (SMSE) levels between –30 dB and –40 dB were achieved. When considering only the relevant parts of the truncated patterns used for stitching, the SMSE values were reduced by an additional 10 dB or more. Furthermore, a comparison with omnidirectional antennas has shown that the directional AUT achieves approximately 6 dB lower SMSE values.

articleTitle: Impact of warm-up on S11 measurements of LoRa antennas using one-port USB-based VNAs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: The stability and accuracy of S11 measurements of an antenna can be significantly influenced by the warm-up process of the Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) used. In the present work, the S11 parameter of two LoRaWAN antennas, working in the range of 915 to 928 MHz, is measured using two different USB-based 1-port VNAs: a PocketVNA and an Anritsu unit. A step-by-step procedure of measurement is proposed in order to evaluate the effect of warm-up the instruments and metric errors are also calculated . It is experimentally shown that warm-up can reduce the variability and increase the accuracy of the measurements.

articleTitle: An Experiment of Virtual Antenna Arrays for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper studies virtual antenna arrays for 5G applications. The study consists of the fabrication of a virtual array to reveal the radiation performance in a real scenario. It is presented with the case of 4, 5, and 6 elements over linear topologies. Each array element comprises one or two antennas built in with a tiny quadcopter drone. The operating frequency is in the lower 5G band of 3.55 GHz. The arrays generate patterns with 11.57 dBi, 12.64 dBi, and 13.51 dBi of directivity. These values can help a swarm of drones communicate with targets at longer distances. The research demonstrates the feasibility of a real virtual antenna array.

articleTitle: Symbolic Regression Applied to Radio Frequency Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This paper explores the application of Symbolic Regression (SR) to data derived from the Okumura propagation model for predicting path loss in wireless systems. Traditional machine learning techniques, such as artificial neural networks and support vector regression, lack the ability to provide mathematical expressions, limiting physical insights. In contrast, SR can generate analytical expressions, offering a more interpretable model. The study compares the SR-derived expression with the Hata model, which also originates from Okumura. Results indicate that the SR model achieves a better fit to the Okumura data, with a RMS error at least 2 dB smaller than that of the Hata model. This demonstrates the potential of SR in enhancing the accuracy and interpretability of path loss predictions.

articleTitle: Mechanically Frequency Reconfigurable Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna based on ENZ Medium for Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: This work proposes a mechanical frequency reconfigurable waveguide-fed cavity-backed slot antenna based on ENZ medium for millimeter wave operation. The antenna air-filled metallic cavity is doped by FR4 dielectric slabs enclosed by four metallic rods to achieve an ENZ medium and fed by a commercial single waveguide-to-coaxial transition through a standard WR28 waveguide. The cavity is semi-cylindrical, providing a semi-omnidirectional radiation pattern at the H-plane. An external sleeve mechanically actuated allows reconfiguring the antenna bandwidth using different slot lengths. The antenna full-wave numerical analyses show reconfigurability from 24.41 to 26.88 GHz, with a gain ranging from 4.80 to 5.15 dBi for eight different slot lengths.

articleTitle: Comparing WINNER Path Loss Models with Machine Learning at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 1st Latin American Conference on Antennas and Propagation (LACAP)
abstract: In this study, the accuracy of various path loss models was evaluated for wireless networks, which are crucial for urban environments with variable propagation conditions. Traditional models such as the Free Space Path Loss (FSPL) model, the modified WINNER model, and the original WINNER model were compared with an advanced machine learning approach using the ADAM algorithm. Data were collected on the campus of the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro (PUCRio) at 5.8 GHz. The machine learning model demonstrated higher accuracy, surpassing the performance of traditional deterministic models.
